dialogs.title: Dialogue — At the bank counter
dialogs.intro: Sarah needs a local bank account to receive her scholarship. She takes a queue number and waits forty minutes before she's called.

notes: **Akaun** = account (from English). *Akaun simpanan* = savings account, *akaun semasa* = current (checking) account. (Indonesian says *rekening* — not used in Malaysia.)

**Pengesahan** = confirmation, verification. *Surat pengesahan* = official confirmation letter. The word family: *sah* (valid, legal), *mengesahkan* (to confirm, certify), *disahkan* (certified). Any document that needs an official stamp is *disahkan*.
**Ruangan** on a form means a **field, box** — not a physical room. *Ruangan nama* = name field. A very Malaysian use that confuses many people at first.
**Kekal** = permanent. *Alamat kekal* = permanent address; a permanent resident is a *pemastautin tetap*.

**Semasa** = current, present. *Alamat semasa* = current address, *isu semasa* = current affairs. ⚠️ It also means "during" (*semasa cuti* = during the holidays), so read the context. It's on every form.

grammars.title: Reading Malaysian official forms
body: Almost every errand in Malaysia starts with a form (*borang*), and the terms are standard everywhere — banks, universities, immigration, hospitals. Learn this table once and you'll never get lost on any form.

head: On the form
English
rows: Single / Married / Widower or divorced man / Widow or divorced woman

after: ⚠️ **Negeri** means **state**, not "country". Malaysia has 13 *negeri* (Selangor, Johor, Pahang…) and 3 *Wilayah Persekutuan* (Federal Territories). "Country" is **negara**. If a form asks for *Negeri*, it wants the state you live in in Malaysia — not your home country.

⚠️ **Jantina** = sex, gender. It's on every Malaysian form. **Taraf** = status, level: *taraf perkahwinan* (marital status), *taraf pendidikan* (level of education), *taraf hidup* (standard of living).

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Baki** = balance, remainder. *Semak baki* = check balance, *baki kredit* = remaining credit. You'll see it on every Malaysian ATM screen.

⚠️ **Faedah** at the bank means **interest**; in general it means **benefit**. *Kadar faedah* = interest rate. Islamic banks use completely different terms (*keuntungan* = profit, *ujrah* = fee), because interest isn't charged. **Caj** (from *charge*) = a charge, fee, and **yuran** = a fee, dues, tuition.

⚠️ **Kredit** = phone credit. *Kredit saya dah habis* = I've run out of credit. **Dalam talian** ("in the line") = online — on every Malaysian government website (*permohonan dalam talian* = online application).
**Kata laluan** = password, literally "word for passing through". Malay coined its own word here rather than borrowing the English one.
**Tempoh sah laku** = validity period. **Tempoh** means a period of time (not "tempo"). *Tempoh sah laku pasport* = passport validity.
**Perkhidmatan** = service. A big word family: *khidmat* (service), *berkhidmat* (to serve), *perkhidmatan awam* (public service, civil service).

blocks.title: Phrases for any counter
items: **Saya nak urus …** — I'd like to sort out …
**Perlu dokumen apa?** — What documents do I need?
**Borang ni kena isi semua ke?** — Do I have to fill in the whole form?
**Ruangan ni maksudnya apa?** — What does this field mean?
**Berapa lama proses ni?** — How long does this take?
**Ada bayaran tak?** — Is there a fee?
**Saya kena datang balik bila?** — When do I need to come back?
**Boleh buat dalam talian tak?** — Can I do it online?

blocks.text: One practical tip for every Malaysian counter: **bring copies** (photocopies) of every document, and bring the originals too. Words you'll hear: *salinan* (copy), *asal* (original), *disahkan* (certified). The full sentence: *Perlu salinan yang disahkan tak?* = "Do you need certified copies?"
